source_citations.title: Incident Classification Standard
source_citations.excerpt: Severity 1 (SEV1) applies when at least 500 customers are affected, when a customer-facing digital or payment service is continuously unavailable for 30 minutes or longer, or when there is credible immediate danger to people. A multi-site closure that prevents essential customer service is also SEV1. Any one threshold is sufficient. An outage lasting 35 or 45 minutes therefore meets the duration threshold even if the impact count is unknown. Suspected impact is validated urgently; classification is precautionary while safety facts are uncertain. Escalation is defined in POL-INC-002 section 2.

source_citations.title: Incident Classification Standard
source_citations.excerpt: Severity 2 (SEV2) applies to 100–499 affected customers, a customer-facing outage of 10–29 minutes, or a single-site disruption without immediate danger. Confirmed duplicate payment capture is at least SEV2, regardless of initial count. Severity 3 (SEV3) is a local degradation affecting fewer than 100 customers with a workaround and no safety or financial-integrity concern. Severity 4 (SEV4) is a minor operational defect with no current customer interruption. If a higher threshold is reached, the higher severity takes priority over these examples.

applicable_internal_policies.text: For Severity 2 (SEV2), notify the Operations Duty Manager and recovery team within 15 minutes, and the Customer Service Lead within 30 minutes. Risk & Compliance must be included within 30 minutes when integrity, safety or suspected data loss is involved. SEV3 and SEV4 are managed by the assigned service owner during the operating shift; record the handover if unresolved. If any SEV1 threshold develops, start the SEV1 clock at that threshold detection and record the upgrade. Lower severity never permits bypassing evidence preservation.

Escalation begins when an incident meets a severity threshold in POL-INC-001. The analyst records when the threshold was first detected and uses that time for notification deadlines. Escalation is a human action: an assistant may recommend recipients and prepare a draft, but a responsible employee sends the notification. A failed delivery does not satisfy the deadline. Record recipient, channel, sent time and acknowledgement. Use the on-call contact directory; this corpus does not contain phone numbers or personal contact details.

For SEV1 customer-impact incidents, issue the first customer notice within 15 minutes of threshold detection and subsequent updates at least every 30 minutes while impact continues. For SEV2, issue the first notice within 30 minutes and update at least every 60 minutes. If no new facts are available, say investigation continues and give the next update time. A restoration notice does not replace a missing earlier update. Record any missed deadline and its reason in the timeline for review.

applicable_internal_policies.text: Severity 2 (SEV2) applies to 100–499 affected customers, a customer-facing outage of 10–29 minutes, or a single-site disruption without immediate danger. Confirmed duplicate payment capture is at least SEV2, regardless of initial count. Severity 3 (SEV3) is a local degradation affecting fewer than 100 customers with a workaround and no safety or financial-integrity concern. Severity 4 (SEV4) is a minor operational defect with no current customer interruption. If a higher threshold is reached, the higher severity takes priority over these examples.

Severity 1 (SEV1) applies when at least 500 customers are affected, when a customer-facing digital or payment service is continuously unavailable for 30 minutes or longer, or when there is credible immediate danger to people. A multi-site closure that prevents essential customer service is also SEV1. Any one threshold is sufficient. An outage lasting 35 or 45 minutes therefore meets the duration threshold even if the impact count is unknown. Suspected impact is validated urgently; classification is precautionary while safety facts are uncertain. Escalation is defined in POL-INC-002 section 2.
